ticket.title: Cancel domain option missing in Billing, customer cannot cancel email accounts and domains
ticket.description:
## Customer report

```text
This is a fault report, not a refund request or billing dispute. The customer (workspace owner) wants to cancel their email accounts and domains. They followed the documented path: Settings > Billing > "Email Accounts & Domains" card > "Cancel" > "Cancel domain". They report the cancel domain option does not show up, so they cannot cancel. We have not seen the screen and do not know exactly what the card shows (no screenshot yet).

What the records show for this workspace:
- Billing shows an active Domain add-on (yearly, $18 per domain, period end about 2026-10-24) and an active Inbox add-on ($8 per inbox per month, 9 inboxes billed on the last three monthly invoices, most recent paid 2026-09-24). Neither add-on has a cancellation date recorded.
- The Pro plan ($185/month) has a cancellation date recorded and ends at period end, about 2026-10-24. Cancelling the plan does not cancel domains or inboxes.
- Billing flags a mismatch: charges succeeded but the product database holds no active subscription status for the organization. Two subscriptions show as active at the payment provider.
- The only domain order (pre-warmed, 6 domains, 18 inboxes, paid 2026-02-24) is marked completed, but 6 domains and 18 inboxes were charged and only 2 domains and 6 inboxes are active. 4 domains are recorded as failed and 12 inboxes as missing. Domain forwarding was not set at purchase for any domain. The feature balance shows domain usage 6 against 3 purchased and inbox usage 18 against 9 purchased.
- No refunds, failed payments or disputed charges are recorded, and the customer has not raised a charge dispute.
- A search of known issues found nothing that clearly matches this exact symptom. An item about domain auto-renewal and a renewal switch in Billing is open (Todo), and an older cancel-domain item is closed. These are leads only.

Needed from Engineering: find out why the Cancel / Cancel domain control is not shown for this workspace's domains, likely tied to the mismatch between billing and the product database and the partly provisioned order. The customer needs a way to end the 6 domains and their inboxes so billing stops. Please also review whether the 9 billed inboxes and the 6 charged domains match what is actually live.
```

relatedSnapshot.title: Domains in failed/Error state have no Cancel option, leaving active inboxes uncancellable
relatedSnapshot.description:
BUG: Yes

EVIDENCE:

* Customer: Name 1 (<email>), workspace **Company One** (`<workspace-slug>`, org `<uuid>`). Reports domains/inboxes still active after cancelling, and no Cancel button in Settings -> Billing -> Email Accounts & Domains.
* Prod DB: Company One has 12 `mail_domain` rows across 2 DFY orders.
  * 6 are `suspended` / "Cancelled by user" (updated 2026-07-20 14:36) - his cancellation on Jul 20 worked for these.
  * 6 are `failed` / "Name 2 waiting for domain/mailboxes": `<domain>`, `<domain>`, `<domain>`, `<domain>`, `<domain>`, `<domain>`.
* Those failed domains still have **15** `mail_inbox` **rows with** `status = active`**,** `connected = true` (3 per domain; the 3 on <domain> are already `error`). Provisioning was recorded as failed at the domain level but the mailboxes exist and are live.
* Root cause in UI: `apps/web/components/billing/email-accounts-domains-card.tsx:44` - `const CANCELLABLE_DOMAIN_STATUSES = ['pending', 'active', 'partial']`. Domains with status `failed` render as "Error" but `isCancellable` is false, so there is no per-domain **Cancel** button and they are excluded from **Cancel all**. No self-serve path exists to remove them or their still-live inboxes.
* Orders: `<uuid>` (status `completed`, "Provisioned 2/6 domains, 6/18 inboxes") and `<uuid>` (status `requires_attention`, "Provisioned 4/6 domains, 12/18 inboxes").
* Billing (Autumn customer `<uuid>` / Stripe `<stripe-id>`): products `Domain` (qty 12) and `Inbox (DFY)` (qty 12) are `past_due` with `canceled_at = 2026-07-20`, current period end **2026-08-18**. $108/mo charge attempts have been failing since 2026-07-18 (8 declines through 2026-07-29).
* Separate question in the same conversation: the **$297 charged 2026-07-27** is the monthly **Pro** plan on a different workspace, **"Test 1"** (`<workspace-slug>`, billing account `<uuid>`, Stripe `<stripe-id>`), billed monthly since 2025-11-27. Not an Company One charge.

POTENTIAL FIX:

* Make provisioning-`failed` domains removable: either add `failed` to `CANCELLABLE_DOMAIN_STATUSES` with a cancel path that also tears down inboxes still `active`/`connected` under that domain, or surface a distinct "Remove" action for error-state domains.
* Reconcile domain vs inbox state: a `failed` domain should not keep `active`, `connected` inboxes. Add a reconciliation job plus a backfill for existing rows.

WHATS NEEDED TO RESOLVE:

* Engineering decision on the cancel/removal path for `failed` domains.
* Manual cleanup for Company One now: remove the 6 failed domains and their 15 active inboxes.
* Confirm no further billing for Company One after 2026-08-18.
* Reply to the customer on the $297 charge (Pro plan on the "Test 1" workspace).

DOCS GAP: The Help Center billing docs (`apps/web/content/docs/workspace-settings/billing.mdx`, "Email Accounts & Domains") describe **Cancel** / **Cancel all** but never explain that domains in an **Error** state show no Cancel button, why, or that support must remove them. Fin AI gave the customer cancel steps he could not follow before handing off.
CUSTOMER CONTEXT: Customer tried to cancel his workspace, emails and domains; the remaining billed items were error-state domains with no Cancel control, so he assumed cancellation had not worked.
SUGGESTED CONTENT: Add an FAQ - "Why is there no Cancel option next to my domain?" - covering the Error/failed provisioning state, its billing impact, and how to get it removed. Also add a note that each workspace bills separately and how to identify which workspace a charge belongs to.
RELATED DOC(S): <url:app.acquisity.ai>

SLACK THREAD: <url:acquisityworkspace.slack.com>
DEVIN SESSION: <url>

relatedSnapshot.title: Add cancel domain and inbox options to billing page
relatedSnapshot.description:
Add functionality on the customer billing page to cancel domain names and inboxes. This should allow customers to manage cancellations for these resources directly from billing.

### Task List

1) Build UI components to enable users to see domains/inboxes on a per-purchase basis
    a) Users should be able to see the domains and inboxes linked to a purchase (which is attached to the order)
    b) If users cancel a domain, we need to automatically cancel the attached inboxes as well
2) Create tRPC endpoint that enables users to selectively cancel to domains/inboxes
    a) We need to update the attached purchase (invoice) to reduce the quantity to reflect new values
3) The Company Two client does have a `deleteEmailAccount` function - we need to disconnect the inbox from the Company Two account on cancellation

Questions:
1) *Should users be able to cancel inboxes, but keep domains?* **No, because Cold Mail Reseller auto cancels a domain when you cancel all of the inboxes for that domains.**

2) *Should the cancellation be immediate, or apply at the next billing cycle?* 

**It should be at the end of the billing cycle. They paid for a full month so we need to deliver the full month, otherwise people will be asking for refunds on unused time.**

Important: Mailbox can only be removed 24 hours before its renewal or expiry date: <url>

So basically we would give the users the option to cancel the domain and then it would cancel and the email boxes with it. And we would NOT give users a prorated refund for any portion of the month they prepaid for email boxes or the domain name.

relatedSnapshot.title: Ask what to do with inboxes and domains when a customer cancels their plan
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a customer cancels their Acquisity plan, the cancel flow asks what should happen to their inboxes and domains. The default is to cancel them too, so customers are not left paying for inboxes they cannot use.

## Problem

Today, cancelling the plan leaves inboxes and domains billing on their own. Customers dispute the charges (for example ENG-12979 and ENG-13645), and we keep paying the provider for inboxes nobody is using.

## User experience

In Settings, Billing, Cancel plan, a new step before confirming:

> **What should happen to your email accounts?**
> You have **36 inboxes on 12 domains** ($288/month). Without a plan, campaigns stop and these inboxes cannot send.
>
> * (selected) **Cancel them with my plan** (recommended). They keep working until {plan end date}, then they are removed. You will not be charged for them again.
> * **Keep them.** They stay warm and keep billing at $288/month, ready if you come back.
>
> \[Back\] \[Cancel plan\]

* Right away: an email confirming the plan end date and what happens to the inboxes.
* 7 days before the end: "Your plan ends in 7 days", with a "Keep my plan" button.
* On the end date: "Your plan has ended", covering paused campaigns, the inbox removal date and how to reactivate.
* Until the end date, a blue sidebar alert: "Your plan ends on {date}", with "Keep my plan".
* A customer who picked "Keep them" can cancel the inboxes later from Billing. A customer who reactivates before the end date keeps everything.

No email or screen names the provider.

## What's included

* The new step, shown only when the workspace has inboxes or domains, with live counts and the monthly total.
* "Cancel them" uses the shared cancel routine in ENG-14252, scheduled for the plan end date: stop charging at period end, switch provider renewal off, keep the inboxes until the paid provider month ends, then remove them.
* The three emails and the blue alert.
* Provider-neutral by design: this ticket only calls ENG-14252's cancel routine, so it is unaffected by moving inboxes to Company Two.

## Blocked by

* ENG-14252, for the shared cancel routine.

Do not run this at the same time as ENG-13360: both add a "stop at plan end" step, and whichever lands second reuses the first. Replaces ENG-7750.

## Done when

* Choosing "Cancel them" schedules inbox and domain cancellation for the plan end date and nothing is billed after it.
* Choosing "Keep them" leaves inbox and domain billing untouched.
* Reactivating before the end date cancels the scheduled removal.
* Counts and prices in the step match Billing.
* The step appears for both Autumn and Whop workspaces.

## Open questions

* Should the default be "Cancel them with my plan"? Recommended: yes. This replaces the earlier July note that preferred asking without a default.

relatedSnapshot.title: Cancelling domains always stops every charge, and never cancels anything else
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a customer, an admin or an automated job cancels domains, every matching domain and mailbox charge must stop at the end of the paid period, and nothing else on the account may be touched. Today a bulk cancel can stop partway and keep charging, and a fallback can cancel the wrong subscription, including the customer's main plan. This ticket builds the one cancel routine every other billing ticket in ENG-13358 reuses.

## Problem

* A customer cancels all their domains. Our records mark everything cancelled, but the billing side stops at the first error or the 5 minute request limit, so the rest keep renewing. The cancelled domains disappear from the page, so the customer cannot retry. 41 workspaces were affected (about 80 domains and 392 mailboxes, roughly $3,136 a month, estimated and not checked against invoices).
* If the first billing call finds no matching subscription, a fallback picks any active subscription on the customer, which can be the main plan.
* The supplier is cancelled immediately, which switches the mailboxes off straight away, while our billing runs to the end of the period. The customer loses service they have paid for.
* Legacy add-ons that cover several domains cannot be targeted, so they keep billing.

Found by the code audit on 28 Sep and not yet reproduced (verify first):

* Whop cancels can report an error after the supplier was already cancelled, so the customer sees a failure and Whop keeps charging.
* A domain whose billing provider differs from the workspace's is cancelled at the supplier, but its billing is skipped while the page shows success.
* Mailbox billing is silently skipped when the order type can't be worked out.
* A partial cancel updates the remaining mailbox count without naming a subscription, which may overbill.
* Cancelling an order with no domains can cancel the whole domain and mailbox products.

## User experience

* A customer cancels one domain or uses "Cancel all". Each domain keeps working and shows "Cancels on {date}" until its paid period ends, then stops. The customer is never charged for it again. The confirm dialog says this, instead of "stop sending immediately".
* If billing cannot be stopped for a domain, the domain stays visible as "Cancellation pending" and we retry automatically. Support sees it in the admin view.
* Nothing on the account other than the selected domains and their mailboxes changes.

## What's included

* One cancel routine used by every cancel path: customer, admin, and the automated tickets in this programme. Each domain's billing cancel is its own retried step with its own saved status, so one failure never blocks the rest and a retry resumes where it stopped.
* Supplier side: switch renewal off with the supplier through a new renewal on/off call, verified in the supplier sandbox first, so the mailboxes run to the end of the paid month. Remove them from sending and mark them cancelled only once the supplier confirms they ended. The immediate supplier cancel stays available for explicit admin use only.
* Find each domain's billing subscription by product, not by a constructed id. Legacy add-ons that cover several domains get a quantity reduction instead of a cancel.
* Remove the fallback that can cancel any subscription.
* Whop and mixed-provider domains follow the same saved-status rules.
* A daily comparison of live billing add-ons against cancelled domains that alerts on any stray add-on.
* Verify and fix the suspected problems listed above.
* Check ENG-13350 (customers get a "something went wrong" error when cancelling inboxes and domains). It is likely the same cancel path; fix it here or record why it is different.

Not included: the one-off cleanup of the remaining stray add-ons, which is listed on the master and needs its own go.

## Blocked by

None: can start immediately.

## Done when

- [ ] Cancelling 12 domains where the 6th billing call fails still stops billing for the other 11, and the 6th is retried and completes.
- [ ] A cancelled domain keeps sending until its paid month ends, then stops, and the supplier shows renewal off.
- [ ] No code path can cancel a subscription that is not the selected domain's or mailbox's.
- [ ] A Whop cancel never reports failure after the supplier was cancelled.
- [ ] The daily comparison finds zero stray add-ons for cancelled domains on a test account.
- [ ] Tests cover partial failure, retry, legacy multi-domain add-ons, Whop and mixed providers.

## Reports

* Intercom conversation, 24 Sep: the owner removed all 6 domains and 18 mailboxes before the cycle and was still charged. Production showed every row cancelled while the billing provider still listed 3 domain and 4 mailbox add-ons with no cancellation, and the renewal invoice charged the 4 mailbox add-ons. Refund: ENG-14253.
* A read-only sweep of 548 billing customers on 28 Sep found 134 add-ons still billing after a customer cancel. 122 were cancelled at end of cycle that day and verified. Still open: 12 add-ons on 2 accounts blocked by an expired Stripe discount; 102 legacy add-ons on accounts with live domains that need a quantity reduction; 50 add-ons on failed domains and 83 on moved domains still billing; 4 add-ons for live domains wrongly scheduled to cancel.
* Replaces ENG-14256, which counted 449 workspaces that had cancelled every domain (3,163 domain and 9,124 mailbox rows) as of 25 Sep.

## Implementation context

* `cancelManagedDomains` (`apps/web/lib/billing/email-management.ts`) marks rows cancelled before the billing adjustment and turns a billing failure into `billingAdjustmentStatus: 'failed'` while still returning success.
* `applyAutumnEndOfCycleCancellation` (`apps/web/lib/billing/providers/autumn/managed-domain-cancellation.ts`) walks domains in a plain sequential loop with no per-domain isolation or retry. The any-subscription fallback is in the same file.
* `getManagedDomainsForCancellation` only returns pending, active or partial domains, so cancelled rows cannot be targeted again.
* Recommended shape: an Inngest job with one retried step per add-on and a per-domain billing-cancel status.
* Existing test harness: `apps/web/tests/lib/billing/email-management-cancel-managed-domains.test.ts`.
* Investigation notes, affected-owner list and the 28 Sep cancel log were produced during the 28 Sep investigation and can be attached on request.

relatedSnapshot.title: Hide Cancel for domains already inactive at CMR
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

Domains already inactive at ColdMailReseller have nothing left to cancel, but the billing page still offered a Cancel action for them — on the per-row button, in "Cancel all", and in the cancellable-domain count.

## Solution

Add `isCancellableDomain` in `email-accounts-domains-card.tsx` — a cancellable status **and** not `cmr_inactive` — and use it for all three: the per-row Cancel, Cancel all, and the cancellable count, so they stay consistent.

## Impact

Customer-facing, cosmetic-to-confusing: a Cancel button that can't meaningfully do anything. Matches the admin-side reasoning in Acquisity/Acquisity#6596, where `overcharged` is deliberately not CMR-cancellable because the domain is already dead at CMR.

## Testing

Typecheck and Biome pass. No unit test added (see below).

## QA

On the billing page, confirm an inactive domain (e.g. `<domain>`) shows no Cancel action, is excluded from "Cancel all", and is not counted in the cancellable total.

## Notes

1 file, +15/-13. Follow-up to Acquisity/Acquisity#6640 (merged). Part of the CMR domain audit series.

relatedSnapshot.title: Make a customer's bulk domain and inbox cancellation resumable so remaining add-ons always stop charging
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A bulk cancellation of managed domains and inboxes stops charging for only part of what was cancelled. The customer's rows are marked cancelled, then their paid add-ons are cancelled one domain at a time, and a stop partway leaves the remaining domain and inbox add-ons renewing against a workspace that has no domains or inboxes left. Because the rows are already cancelled, the customer cannot run the cancellation again.

## Problem

Customer-initiated cancellation through Settings, Billing, Email Accounts & Domains (single domain or Cancel all) is not durable: the UI returns success, the domains and inboxes read as cancelled, and yet part of the paid add-ons keeps billing. Support has to finish the job by hand.

## Root cause

`cancelManagedDomains` (apps/web/lib/billing/email-management.ts) marks the rows cancelled through `markManagedDomainCancelled` before applying the billing adjustment, and swallows the adjustment failure into `billingAdjustmentStatus: 'failed'` while still returning a success result. `applyAutumnEndOfCycleCancellation` (apps/web/lib/billing/providers/autumn/managed-domain-cancellation.ts) then walks the cancelled domains in a plain sequential loop with `cancelPlanForDomain`, which has no per-domain error isolation and no retry, so a failure or a killed request leaves the remaining add-ons untouched. `getManagedDomainsForCancellation` only considers domains in pending, active or partial, so the suspended rows cannot be targeted again.

## Blast radius

449 workspaces have user-cancelled every managed domain with no domain left in a cancellable status (136 in the last 45 days, 33 in the last 14 days), counted 2026-09-25 in production: 3163 cancelled domain rows and 9124 cancelled inbox rows. A same-day sample of six of those workspaces read in the billing provider found three still carrying at least one add-on subscription with no cancellation recorded. Exact failing count is not readable from production alone because the failure is visible only in provider state.

## Proposed fix

Make the cancellation resumable: isolate each domain's provider cancellation so one failure cannot abort the rest, retry the domains that failed, and keep the local status recoverable (a distinct in-progress or retryable state instead of a terminal cancelled one) so the same request or the customer can complete it. The cancellation should report failure the customer can act on when any add-on is left billing.

## Regression seam

The bulk cancellation entry point with a provider that fails for one domain: today the other domains are left uncancelled and the call still reports success; afterwards every add-on of every cancelled domain ends cancelled, or the rows stay re-cancellable and the failure is reported. Existing harness: apps/web/tests/lib/billing/email-management-cancel-managed-domains.test.ts.

## Done when

* One failing domain no longer prevents the remaining domains' add-ons from being cancelled.
* A partially completed cancellation leaves the affected rows re-cancellable and tells the user, instead of reading as fully cancelled.
* A regression test proves both behaviours at the bulk cancellation entry point.

## Reports

Customer report for this instance: ENG-14252.

Bounded context: customer opened with "cancel all subscriptions and billing", then reported he has never had any inboxes or domains but is being charged for both; cancelling his legacy plan lowered the next bill by only $1; Manage Billing shows no subscription list to cancel; the remaining line item is labelled "inbox - inboxes - 18 x 8". He was escalated to a human and has had no answer.

Claim: 18 inboxes were charged at $8/month from 2025-12-03 to date, and $107.77 for 6 pre-warmed domains, but the workspace holds no domains or inboxes, has no outreach account connected, and the purchase record shows 0 of 18 mailbox creations succeeded, so the customer paid for a year of inbox capacity that never existed and has no self-serve control to stop the recurring charge.

Ask bucket: overcharged (money).

Verified money (Stripe, <stripe-id>): $1,554.08 USD collected across 12 paid invoices; nothing refunded; no credit notes; balance 0; no dispute. Of that, $1,436.31 is the 18-inbox charge (first month prorated $140.31 plus nine months at $144.00) and $107.77 is the domain year; $10.00 is the Legacy plan.

Forward exposure: $145.00 due 2026-10-02 and $108.00 due 2026-12-02, then $145.00 monthly, with no in-product cancellation path.

Why there is no cancel path (current code): the Billing page card renders from org mail_domain rows only and shows "No managed domains" when there are none, offering no Cancel control; cancellation runs through cancelManagedDomains, which returns "Domain is not managed by this workspace" when no mail_domain row exists. Cancelling the named plan product cancels only that product, which is the $1 reduction the customer saw. Repository HEAD read: f0228bab1e57b287a17a66e2e042abc3de8191dd.

Discretion: needs-human. All three systems of record agree the add-ons are live and paid, so this is not a sync fault; the divergence is between what was paid for and what exists in the workspace. No prior approval or promise exists in the conversation or the request, so the amount decision is a person's.

Proposed human action (proposal, not a promise):

1. Cancel the live Inbox add-on ($8 x 18) and the Domain add-on on billing account 7de4ed09.../Stripe subscription <stripe-id> before the 2026-10-02 renewal, so the October and December charges cannot land.
2. Decide the refund: $1,436.31 for inbox capacity never created plus an amount for the domain year the customer never had visible, out of $1,554.08 collected. No refund or credit has been issued.
3. Tell the customer, because he has had no answer since Fin AI escalated him on 2026-09-29.

Unverified on this ticket: the customer's purchase intent at signup; whether the December 2025 order flow code matches today's HEAD, so no failing function is attributed; the provider-side cancellation record for these six domains (the cancellation log table starts 2026-08-01 and holds no row for them).

relatedSnapshot.title: Managed domain cancellation fails with a generic error when the domain and inbox order_id mismatch
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Cancelling a managed email domain from Billing → Email Accounts & Domains fails with a generic "something went wrong" error when the domain's `order_id` does not match its inboxes' `order_id`. The provider-side cancellation can still run, but the local records never update, so the domain stays active and the customer keeps being billed for a domain they want gone.

## Problem

A customer cancels a managed domain and its inboxes. The cancel returns a generic error and the domain remains active, so the customer cannot stop being billed for it.

## Root cause

`markManagedDomainCancelled` in `apps/web/lib/billing/email-management.ts` updates `mail_inbox` rows `WHERE order_id = <the domain's order_id>`. When the `mail_domain` row's `order_id` differs from its inboxes' `order_id`, zero inboxes match, and the function throws "Failed to mark managed domain inboxes as cancelled" because `expectedInboxCount > 0`. That throw is collected as a mark failure and re-thrown as "Provider cancellation completed … but failed to update local cancellation records", which `apps/web/trpc/routers/outreach/email-accounts.ts` turns into `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` "Failed to cancel selected managed domains".

## Blast radius

Confirmed: 1 org / 1 domain. Deterministic exposure: 3 orgs / 5 domains have at least one inbox whose `order_id` differs from the domain's `order_id` among cancellable (`active`/`pending`/`partial`) domains (counted 2026-09-01). Of those, 2 domains hard-fail (zero inboxes match the domain order_id) and 3 partially update.

```sql
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT md.organization_id), COUNT(DISTINCT md.id)
FROM mail_domain md
JOIN mail_inbox mi ON mi.domain_id = md.id AND mi.organization_id = md.organization_id
WHERE md.status IN ('active','pending','partial')
  AND mi.order_id IS DISTINCT FROM md.order_id;
```

## Proposed fix

Reconcile the `order_id` mismatch so a domain and its inboxes share a consistent `order_id`, and make `markManagedDomainCancelled` tolerant of the mismatch (update inboxes by `domain_id` rather than requiring `order_id` to match, or reconcile before cancelling). Add a reconciliation/backfill for existing mismatched rows.

## What's included

* Stop cancellation from hard-failing on an `order_id` mismatch.
* Backfill/reconcile existing mismatched rows.
* A regression test for the zero-match condition.

## Regression seam

`markManagedDomainCancelled` in `apps/web/lib/billing/email-management.ts`. Red: cancelling a domain whose inboxes carry a different `order_id` throws and the cancel fails. Green: the same domain cancels successfully and both the domain and its inboxes are marked cancelled.

## Done when

* Cancelling a domain with a mismatched inbox `order_id` succeeds and marks the domain and all its inboxes cancelled.
* Existing mismatched rows are reconciled.
* A regression test proves the zero-match condition no longer throws.

## Reports

* ENG-13350

relatedSnapshot.title: Customer's cancellation request left a $129 past-due subscription with a retry scheduled, on the billing account they never cancelled
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom source: <url:app.intercom.com>

Conversation context: Contact (Name 11, <email>) opened on 2026-09-30 asking to cancel his domains and Cold Email Agent (AI SDR) client and to stop being billed. Fin AI answered with self-serve cancellation steps and closed the conversation; the contact reopened it and asked for a human. His final message: "I've gone through the process of cancelling one of the subaccouts (Company Four) and the domains/inboxes and further billing. However, I was attempted to be billed yesterday and it did not go through. I want the charges to be cancelled and not attempted to bill me again." No amount, invoice id, or date was named. No prior approval, promise, coupon, or discretionary credit appears anywhere in the thread.

Account: this contact is the owner of two workspaces. Company Four, Inc. (created 2026-05-20) carries the domains, inboxes and paid plan. Name 11's Workspace (created 2025-07-14) is the personal $1 Legacy workspace he enrolled first.

Ask (classify_ask): money, bucket 'overcharged'. Two distinct things are mixed in one message: stopping a failed charge and its retry, and a prior billing discrepancy he has never itemized.

## Evidence

Systems of record, read in order.

PlanetScale (acquisity / main):

* Company Four billing account 10e96d6f-...: subscriptionStatus null, subscriptionPlan null, domains balance 0, inboxes balance 0, no credit transactions. Its 10 mail_domain rows are all suspended as of 2026-09-30T00:26:57Z.
* The suspended domains sit under domain_purchase_order d9aaa5e6-... (created 2026-05-27, 10 domains ordered, 29/30 inboxes provisioned, completed 2026-05-28). A second order d0d8aa9b-... (2026-07-25, 20 domains) was cancelled by the user and never paid, so it never billed.
* Name 11's Workspace, billing account 32f7330c-..., is unchanged and still active.

Autumn:

* Company Four (billing account 10e96d6f-...): one subscription, plan legacy_pro at $129/month, status active, past_due true, canceled_at 1790727969812 (2026-09-30, about 22:26 UTC, roughly 18 minutes before the contact's last Intercom message), expires_at 1793135024000, current_period_end 2026-10-27. The cancel was requested inside the product. No cancellations exist for the 10 domain line items or the 10 inbox line items, which is why the domains show suspended rather than cancelled.
* Name 11's Workspace (billing account 32f7330c-...): plan legacy at $1/month, active, its own Stripe customer <stripe-id>. It kept billing $1/month in Aug and Sep 2026.

Stripe:

* Company Four, <stripe-id>, is delinquent and carries two subscriptions and two separate billing streams:
  * <stripe-id>, Legacy Pro $129/month. cancel_at 1793135024, so its next charge has already been stopped. Invoice <stripe-id> (OPDYCP6F-0010), 12900 USD, status open, amount_paid 0, attempt_count 1, next_payment_attempt 1790769908. That scheduled retry is the billing attempt the contact is asking us to stop. The period 2026-08-28 to 2026-09-27 was already collected earlier on charge <stripe-id> on 2026-09-08 after eight declines.
  * A second Legacy Pro subscription stream under a separate Stripe subscription, invoice OPDYCP6F-0009 (18000 USD, open, attempt_count 9) plus a domain/inbox stream that last billed 18000 USD on invoice OPDYCP6F-0007 (paid 2026-08-24).
  * Every open charge on this customer is a failed attempt: status failed, card_declined, insufficient_funds (issuer decline code 51), amount_captured 0. No money was collected on any of them.
  * Total actually taken from this account in Aug and Sep 2026: 18000 + 12900 = 30900 USD. No refunds and no credit notes exist on the account.
* Name 11's Workspace, <stripe-id>, is current and not delinquent.

Name 12:

* No Inngest or Sentry lane was needed to explain the charge itself; the divergence is fully explained by the reads above.

## First divergent hop

Not a system-to-system break: Stripe, Autumn and the workspace disagree about nothing. The gap is between the contact's belief about what he cancelled and what the product cancelled. He cancelled the plan on the Company Four workspace, which set the subscription to cancel at period end, and the domains/inboxes were suspended, but the already-issued open invoice for the running period still has a retry scheduled, and the domain/inbox line items were never cancelled as subscriptions.

## Verification

The in-app billing page he was looking at shows the open $129 charge while the plan already reads as cancelled, which is exactly the "billing error/discrepancy" he reported. That reading is consistent with the Stripe state and is a product presentation issue, not a data error.

## What is not established

What the earlier discrepancy he referred to on 2026-09-30 consisted of. He never named an amount, invoice, or date, and nothing in the account shows a charge that overstates what he was entitled to for the periods billed. The outstanding retry and the residual domain/inbox subscription state are the only unresolved money items.

## Unblock and open human decision

Two separate things need a human, and neither is money we can move automatically:

1. Stop the next charge. Cancel the two open invoices' retry (next_payment_attempt 1790769908 on invoice <stripe-id>) and cancel the domain/inbox line items that are still live on the Company Five billing account so nothing is attempted again.
2. Decide the old discrepancy. Once he names what he believes is wrong, decide whether any refund is owed. Nothing collected after the cancellation date is refundable, because nothing was collected after it.
